feedback: Written before this candidate races, so it states no outcome. The candidate is a controlled test against iteration 1 (score 356.6, the best raced so far). It keeps the iteration 1 controller (kp 2.5, kd 0.8, ki 0.02) and sensor_size 0.012, widens the sensor span from ±0.04 to ±0.06 m, and lowers base_speed from 1.3 to 1.1. Iteration 2 (score 270.4) changed four things at once, so its failure could not be attributed. This design isolates the span effect. Two points in the rationale need correction. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.18/4) = 0.06 m, not 0.0575 m, so the body width gives no extra margin. Also, a 0.03 m sensor spacing with 0.012 m footprints still leaves a gap of 0.018 m, which is smaller than the 0.025 m tape, so a sensor always sees tape. The speed cut is the larger risk. Iteration 1 oval finished in 1.89 s at 1.3, so scaling by 1.3/1.1 predicts about 2.2 s, which is inside the 3 s limit. If the oval mean time comes back above 2.5 s, the speed cut has gone too far. Next race: if s-bend and slalom still go off track with line_loss_events near 1 and max_error at or above 0.06 m, the span is not the limiting factor, so raise kd from 0.8 to about 1.0 to damp the swing before changing kp. If the oval finish time is above 2.5 s, raise base_speed to about 1.2. If the span widening alone brings max_error on the bends below 0.05 m, keep the span and tune speed upward toward 1.3 to recover oval time.
requested_changes: If s-bend or slalom still leave the line with line_loss_events near 1 and max_error at or above 0.06 m: raise kd from 0.8 to about 1.0 (keeping kp 2.5, ki 0.02) to damp the swing. Iteration 2 showed kd 1.0 kept steering_oscillation near 0.27, so the damping is not harmful.

If oval completion is above 0.9 but mean completion_time is above 2.5 s: raise base_speed from 1.1 to about 1.2 to recover time while keeping the wider span. Iteration 1 finished the oval in 1.89 s at 1.3.
If bend max_error falls below 0.05 m with progress above 0.5: keep the ±0.06 m span and return base_speed toward 1.3, since the span rather than the speed was limiting the bends.
